expectations.text: DSL validates cleanly with the Structurizr CLI (Docker) — or, if Docker is unavailable, the response says plainly it was not validated
expectations.evidence: Re-validated by the grader: `structurizr/structurizr validate` exit 0.

expectations.text: Container view has exactly the SPA, the API and PostgreSQL — no Kubernetes, pod, Docker, EKS, ALB or WAF element on it
expectations.evidence: Container view includes only spa, api, db (containers of `agenda`); WAF/ALB/EKS/pod live under `producao`.

expectations.text: Production deployment nests AWS → EKS → Kubernetes cluster → pod (instances 3) → (Docker container) → API instance, and PostgreSQL is deployed under an RDS node
expectations.evidence: Nesting is AWS → `plataforma` (technology 'Amazon EKS') → 'Pod da API' (instances 3) → instanceOf. The EKS service and the Kubernetes cluster are merged into one node and the Docker-container layer is skipped; the official EKS example nests AWS → EKS → cluster → pod → container. Acceptable simplification, but not the reference shape. PostgreSQL under `rds` OK.

expectations.text: ALB and WAF are infrastructureNodes inside the production environment (not deploymentNodes, not containers)
expectations.evidence: `waf = infrastructureNode "AWS WAF"` and `alb = infrastructureNode "Application Load Balancer"` inside `aws`.

expectations.text: The SPA→API relationship is rerouted through WAF and ALB in the deployment environment using `-/>` (or an equivalent explicit reroute), so the deployment view shows SPA → WAF → ALB → API
expectations.evidence: `agenda.spa -/> agenda.api { spa -> aws.waf; aws.waf -> aws.alb; aws.alb -> agenda.api }`.

expectations.text: No invented architecture: no extra containers, systems or relationships beyond the spec (cosmetic defaults allowed)
expectations.evidence: Only stated elements/relationships; `WebBrowser` tag and styles are cosmetic. Region and SPA hosting left as open questions.
